declarations.description:
Base class every component extends.

Kept intentionally thin: universal resets/properties and the registration
contract only. Behavior that not every component needs (open/close, focus
delegation, form association, ...) belongs in a mixin from `src/mixins`.
Custom events are dispatched as typed `Event` subclasses from
`src/events`, not through a generic base-class `emit()` helper — see
`src/events/modal-close.ts` for the pattern.

Classes never register themselves (ADR 0001, D1): `defineComponents()`
registers a subclass per prefix (`u-button`, `acme-button`, ...) and
hands it the tag names of its registration through `tagNames`.
declarations.name: DSBaseElement

members.name: componentName
members.description:
Name of the component in the catalog, without any tag prefix: the
registered tag is `<prefix>-<componentName>`. Every concrete component
sets it; abstract bases (e.g. `ButtonBase`) don't.

members.name: dependencies
members.description:
Components this one renders (ADR 0001, D2): `defineComponents()`
registers them too, and `tagFor()` resolves their tag. Never hard-code
another component's tag in a template, nor create one with
`document.createElement` — a brand's override would be bypassed.

declarations.description:
Fired by `modal` before it closes at the user's request: its close button,
Escape, a click outside (`closedby="any"`), `requestClose()` or the
`--request-close` command. `preventDefault()` keeps it open, for unsaved
changes for instance. Not cancelable when the browser closes it anyway:
Escape pressed again without any interaction in between.
declarations.name: ModalCancelEvent

declarations.description:
Fired by `modal` when its dialog closes, whatever the cause: its close
button, Escape, a click outside, a command, a method, or `open` set to
`false`. The native `close` event of the inner `<dialog>` doesn't leave the
shadow root.
declarations.name: ModalCloseEvent

members.name: value
members.description:
The value the modal closed with, its `returnValue`: the `value` of the
button that sent `--close` or `--request-close`, or the argument of
`close()` or `requestClose()`. Empty when dismissed without one, by
Escape for instance. Not `returnValue`: `Event` has a legacy one.

members.name: handleCommand
members.description: Runs a command sent to the component.

declarations.description:
Mixin: lets a component take commands from invoker buttons (Invoker
Commands): a native `<button commandfor="id" command="--name">`, or a
component with `withInvoker` (`button`).

The browser runs a built-in command (`show-modal`) only on a native
`<dialog>` or popover, and never sends it to a custom element. A component
takes custom commands, prefixed with `--`.

Where Invoker Commands are missing, the first connected component loads
invokers-polyfill: the page's native invoker buttons need it too.
declarations.name: withCommands

members.name: handleCommand
members.description:
Runs a command sent to the component: `event.command` is its name,
`event.source` the button, retargeted to its host. Does nothing by
default. Handle the component's `--` commands and ignore the others:
the polyfill also sends built-in ones.

members.name: cancelExitTransition
members.description: Stops an exit transition under way: `element` stays open.

declarations.description:
Mixin: animates the exit of a top-layer element of the shadow root, a
`<dialog>` or a popover, in every browser.

The component's CSS writes the transition: the closed state on the
element, the open state on `[open]` or `:popover-open` followed by
`:where(:not([data-closing]))`, the entry in `@starting-style`, and
`display` and `overlay` among the transitioned properties. Where `overlay`
is missing, `closeWithTransition()` sets `data-closing` first: the element
reaches its closed state in the top layer, then closes.
declarations.name: withExitTransition

members.name: closeWithTransition
members.description:
Closes `element` once its exit transition ends: `close` closes it
(`dialog.close()`, `hidePopover()`). Without transition, as with
reduced motion, it closes at once. Resolves when closed, or when
`cancelExitTransition()` kept it open.

declarations.description:
Mixin: Attaches `ElementInternals` and exposes it as `this.internals`.

`attachInternals()` can only be called once per element, so any component
that needs form participation (`internals.form`, `setFormValue`, validity)
or `:state()` custom states should apply this mixin and read `this.internals`
— never call `this.attachInternals()` directly.
declarations.name: withInternals

Wraps `internals.states` so components can toggle `:state(x)` selectors
(e.g. `:state(open)`) instead of reflecting extra boolean attributes.
A no-op where `:state()` is unsupported (see `supportsCustomStates`), so
`:state()` styling must stay an enhancement — reflect an attribute too
when the state is needed for the component to look right.

declarations.description:
Mixin: makes a component that renders a native `<button>` an invoker, as
`<button commandfor command>` is (Invoker Commands). The component takes
`commandfor` and `command`, and hands them to its native button: the
browser sends the command, runs the built-in ones on a native `<dialog>`
or popover, and retargets `event.source` to the host.

Where Invoker Commands are missing, the first component with a `command`
loads invokers-polyfill.

An alert component that displays a message to the user.

The icon of its type comes first: the icon of the same name, from the
`icon` component of its registration. It's decorative: the type is in the
role and the colors, and the message says it.

Its container is a live region (`role="status"` or `"alert"`, from
`type`). Screen readers announce what is added to a live region, not what
it already held when it appeared, so the message is revealed 100 ms after
the alert is first rendered: an alert inserted with its message is
announced too. Until then the message is laid out (nothing moves) but
invisible.

declarations.description:
Shared base of the form fields, `text-field` and `textarea`: a label, an
optional hint, a native control and its error message. Abstract: extend
`TextField` or `Textarea`, or write a field with `renderControl()`. The
label stays in the shadow root of its control: an `id` doesn't cross a
shadow root (ADR 0007).

A field takes part in its form like a native control: it submits `value`
under `name`, blocks the submission while invalid, follows the form's
reset and a `<fieldset disabled>`.

Validation is the browser's, on the native control, plus
`setCustomValidity()`. The error shows once the user has changed the value
and left the field, or once validation has run (a submission attempt,
`checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`), then follows each keystroke. The
message is the browser's, in the browser's language: give `error-message`
to write it in the page's language. A message set with
`setCustomValidity()` comes first.

Its `input` and `change` events are those of a native control, on the
host: frameworks bind `value` as they would on an `<input>` (`v-model` in
Vue).

declarations.description:
An icon of the set of its registration, by name (ADR 0005).

The set of the base is `@unicorne/icons`: one module per icon, loaded the
first time an icon renders, so a page downloads only the icons it shows.
The box keeps its size while the icon loads, and `updateComplete` resolves
once the icon is rendered. The icon takes the color of the text
(`currentColor`).

Without `label`, the icon is decorative: assistive technologies ignore it.
Give a `label` to an icon that carries meaning on its own.

declarations.description:
A modal dialog. Built on the native `<dialog>`: the browser provides the
backdrop, makes the rest of the page inert, closes it on Escape and gives
the focus back to the element that had it.

Open it from a button, without script: `<u-button commandfor="id"
command="--show-modal">`, or a native `<button>` with the same attributes.
The commands are `--show-modal`, `--close` and `--request-close`; the last
two take the button's `value` as `returnValue`. From script, call
`showModal()`, `close()` or `requestClose()`, or set `open`.

It enters and leaves with a fade and a slight scale, set by its tokens.
With reduced motion, it appears and disappears at once.

members.name: focusInitial
members.description:
Gives the focus as the dialog's focusing steps would, across the slot:
to the content's `autofocus` element, or else to the close button.
Firefox and Safari only look for `autofocus` in the shadow root. Opened
on its first render, the modal has a close button without its native
`<button>` yet, and the dialog keeps the focus: focus again once the
element has rendered, unless the focus moved meanwhile.

members.name: handleDialogCancel
members.description:

Closes through `u-cancel` and the exit transition, not at once.

members.name: handleDialogClose

single place that keeps `open` truthful to the actual dialog state and
announces the closing.

members.name: isOutside

members.name: handlePointerUp
members.description:

outside: a text selection that ends on the backdrop doesn't close it.

members.name: closeWithTransition
members.description:
Closes `element` once its exit transition ends: `close` closes it
(`dialog.close()`, `hidePopover()`). Without transition, as with
reduced motion, it closes at once. Resolves when closed, or when
`cancelExitTransition()` kept it open.
